The writer effectively uses sensory details—primarily sight and sound—to create a tangible and believable environment. Visually, the reader is given specific details such as the "zwei magern Schimmeln" (two skinny white horses), the rapeseed trickling out of the small holes and cracks in the poorly tied sacks, and the precise architectural layout of the hallway divided by wooden pillars and hammocks. Auditorily, the scene comes to life with the farmhand's sleepy "Hüh" (giddyup) and the sound of the wagon as it "klapperte" (clattered/rattled) down the road. These details ground the narrative in a realistic, physical world.
